Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: Can MVFA's few-shot fusion be made inductive — scoring each image on its own, without the test-set min-max normalisation of the released code — without losing AUROC, and does this give a threshold that transfers to unseen modalities? The inductive fusion standardises each branch with leave-one-out statistics of the K normal support images (each support's zero-shot map, and its few-shot map against a memory bank built from the other K-1 supports, pooled over patches and levels), adds the standardised branches, and pools the fused map with the mean of its top 2% pixels; the threshold is the 95th percentile of the supports' leave-one-out image scores. Primary outcome: image- and pixel-level AUROC of inductive versus transductive fusion on every held-out modality and K in {2, 4, 8, 16}. Motivating measurement: the spread of the transductive AUROC across random test subsets and at 10% and 50% prevalence. Secondary outcomes: sensitivity, realised specificity, F1 and expected calibration error at the support-derived threshold. We also record whether the few-shot baselines compared in the target paper (APRIL-GAN, WinCLIP) normalise over the test set in their public code, to judge how widely the finding applies.

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Brown-corrected Fisher fusion: dependence-adjusted p-value combination estimated from support normals, with region-mass pooling
SUMMARY: Keep Fisher's powerful combination of per-level, per-branch support p-values but correct its null distribution for the dependence between MVFA's levels and branches using Brown's method with covariances estimated on the support normals, then pool by region mass.
HYPOTHESIS: Brown-corrected Fisher fusion keeps realised false-positive rates within 3 points of nominal (like harmonic-mean fusion) while retaining Fisher's image AUROC within 0.3 points, giving at least 0.5 AUROC points more than harmonic-mean fusion on held-out BMAD modalities with K >= 4.
RATIONALE: The two parents trade power for validity: Fisher is powerful but anti-conservative for correlated evidence, the harmonic mean p-value is valid under dependence but can lose power. Brown's method keeps Fisher's statistic and rescales its chi-square null using the covariance of the -2 log p terms, which can be estimated from the support normals' leave-one-out p-values — no labels needed. This combines the strength of each parent and the shared region-mass pooling.
METHOD: 1) Per-pixel empirical p-values p_bl (8 terms) from support LOO nulls. 2) Estimate the covariance of -2 log p_bl across pixels of support normals (LOO), giving Brown's scale c and degrees of freedom f: c = Var(X)/(2E[X]), f = 2E[X]^2/Var(X), with E[X] = 16 under independence. 3) Pixel statistic: Brown p-value = 1 - F_chi2(X/c; f); use -log of it as the pixel map. 4) Region-mass pooling and support-derived thresholds as in the parents. 5) Code: scoring.py brown_fisher(); test_few.py per image.
EXPERIMENT: BMAD leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); MVFA checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits and the MVFA baseline re-run the same way; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: Fisher + region mass; harmonic-mean + region mass; LOO-Z + region mass. Metrics: realised FPR at 1% and 5%, sensitivity, image/pixel AUROC, PRO, estimated c and f per modality. Falsification: FPR not within 3 points or AUROC below harmonic-mean fusion.

Idea B:
TITLE: Support-bootstrap uncertainty: deciding on the lower confidence bound of a per-image MVFA score
SUMMARY: Resample the K support normals with replacement to obtain a distribution of each test image's support-normalised score, and flag an image only when the lower confidence bound exceeds the threshold, giving per-image uncertainty that grows as K shrinks.
HYPOTHESIS: Using the 10th-percentile bootstrap bound reduces false positives at K = 2 and K = 4 by at least 30% relative to the point estimate at the same threshold, with sensitivity loss below 10 points, and the bootstrap interval width correlates with per-image error (Spearman rho >= 0.3).
RATIONALE: By analogy with ensemble forecasting, where the spread of an ensemble indicates the reliability of a prediction, the dependence of a per-image score on which few supports were drawn is itself the main source of uncertainty in MVFA's few-shot mode (one fixed draw in the released code). Bootstrapping the supports quantifies it per image at no labelling cost, and deciding on a lower bound turns that uncertainty into fewer false alarms where evidence is thin.
METHOD: 1) B = 30 bootstrap resamples of the K supports; for each, recompute support statistics (LOO-Z) and the region-mass image score of the test image. 2) Point score = median; lower bound = 10th percentile. 3) Threshold from support LOO scores as before. 4) Cost: memory banks are reused, only statistics recomputed; few-shot distances computed once per support image and indexed. 5) Code: scoring.py bootstrap_scores().
EXPERIMENT: BMAD leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); MVFA checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits and the MVFA baseline re-run the same way; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: LOO-Z + region mass point estimate; harmonic-mean fusion. Metrics: FP and sensitivity at the threshold, interval width vs error correlation, image AUROC of median score. Falsification: no FP reduction at K <= 4.

WINNER=<A | B | TIE>
